newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Spectrum completes Ban Phuc 2nd drilling.
newsitem.headline: Spectrum completes Ban Phuc 2nd drilling.

text.p: Spectrum Resources said on Wednesday its second drilling program at Ban Phuc had been successfully completed.

A resource of approximately one million tonnes grading 3.5 percent nickel, 1.3 percent copper and 0.1 percent cobalt had previously been defined at Ban Phuc based on earlier drilling by the Vietnamese.
Spectrum has a 70 percent stake in Ban Phuc.
Spectrum said BP97-6 assayed 1.38 percent Ni and 0.22 percent Cu over 40 metres, including a 12 metre section grading 2.02 percent Ni.
This hole had given similar results to BP96-7 and old Vietnamese hole LK46 which both intersected wide zones of similar grade mineralization within the ultrabasic body.
"This intersection enhances the probability of converting the low grade inferred resource into indicated reserves," Spectrum said in a statement.

Within the massive sulphide zone some good results were obtained from BP97-2 which intersected 9m of 2.55 percent Ni and 1.3 percent Cu, and BP97-13 which intersected 5.10m at 2.09 percent Ni and 0.28 percent Cu.

Spectrum said although the 4m wide intersection of 1.35 percent Ni in BP97-15 is only a moderate result, it was of particular importance as it represented the top of a lens of mineralization plunging to the west.
The possibility existed of substantially increased tonnage in that lens, it said.
There were indications that holes in BP97-14 and BP97-13 had not penetrated the full width of the mineralization.
"Both holes appear to have been stopped too soon," the company said.
